fig1_mandelstam.svg: The three Mandelstam invariants of $2\to2$ equal-mass scattering from mandelstam$(\sqrt{s}{=}5,\theta,m{=}1)$: $s$ is fixed by the CM energy while $t,u$ slide linearly in $\cos\theta$ (both $\le 0$, spacelike momentum transfer). Their sum (dashed) stays pinned at $s+t+u=4m^2$ for every angle — the kinematic identity that leaves only two independent invariants.
fig2_propagator.svg: The scalar Feynman propagator $D_F=i/(p^2-m^2+i\epsilon)$ from propagator(), evaluated on 4-vectors swept through the invariant $x=p^2-m^2$ (regulator $\epsilon=0.3$). $\mathrm{Re}\,D_F$ is a Lorentzian of width $\epsilon$ peaking at the on-shell pole $x=0$ (a nascent $\pi\delta(x)$), while $\mathrm{Im}\,D_F$ is the dispersive principal value $\to 1/x$ off shell — the $i\epsilon$ causal prescription that sits on every internal line.
